title: The Latest Time to Catch a Bus
statement:
Buses leave a station at the times listed in `buses`, and other riders reach the station at the times listed in `passengers`. No two buses share a departure time and no two riders share an arrival time. Each bus holds at most `capacity` people.

When a bus departs at time `x`, everyone who reached the station at time `x` or earlier and has not boarded yet stands in a queue ordered by arrival time; the first `capacity` people in that queue get on (all of them if there are fewer). You also want to ride one of the buses, and you join the queue by your arrival time like everyone else.

Return the latest integer time at which you can arrive and still get on a bus. You are not allowed to arrive at exactly the same time as any rider in `passengers`. Neither array is necessarily sorted.
constraints: All values in buses are distinct
All values in passengers are distinct
signature: int latestTimeCatchTheBus(int[] buses, int[] passengers, int capacity)
notes:
## Intuition

A brute force would try every arrival time and replay the whole boarding process, which is far too slow for times up to 10^9. Instead, replay the boarding just once with everybody else. Only the last bus matters for you: arriving later than its departure is useless, and any earlier bus leaves before the last one. If the last bus leaves with a free seat, you could arrive right at its departure; if it is full, you must arrive before the last person who got on it. Either way, step back past any riders already holding that exact minute.

## Approach

1. Sort `buses` and `passengers`.
2. Walk the buses with a pointer `next` into the riders. For each `departure`, reset `boarded` and let riders with time `<= departure` on until the bus is full.
3. After the loop, `last = next - 1` is the final rider who boarded. If the last bus still had room, start `answer` at its departure time; otherwise start at `passengers[last]`.
4. While `passengers[last]` equals `answer`, that minute is taken: decrease `answer` and move `last` back one.
5. Return `answer`.

## Example 1, step by step

`buses = [10, 20]`, `passengers = [2, 17, 18, 19]`, `capacity = 2`. The bus at 10 takes rider 2. The bus at 20 takes 17 and 18 and is full, so `next = 3`, `last = 2` and `answer = 18`. Minute 18 is taken, so `answer = 17`; 17 is taken too, so `answer = 16`. Rider 2 does not match, and the answer is `16`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n + m log m) for the sorts; the boarding walk and the step-back are linear.
- Space: O(1) beyond the sorts.

## Pitfalls

- `boarded` must describe the **last** bus only, so reset it for every bus.
- When the last bus is full you must beat its last rider, not simply arrive at the departure time.
- Stepping back must compare against consecutive boarded riders, which works because `passengers` is sorted.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `next` | index of the first rider who has not boarded yet |
| `boarded` | riders who got on the current bus |
| `departure` | departure time of the current bus |
| `last` | index of the boarded rider being compared with `answer` |
| `answer` | the candidate arrival time |

narration.2: Sort the departures so the buses are processed in the order they leave.
narration.3: Sort the riders so the queue is simply the array order.
narration.4: next points at the first rider still waiting or not yet arrived.
narration.7: Handle the buses one by one, earliest first.
narration.9: Board riders while there is a seat and the next rider arrived by the departure time.
narration.10: That rider gets on, so move to the following one.
narration.15: last is the index of the final rider who boarded any bus.
narration.16: With a free seat on the last bus you can come at its departure; otherwise you must replace its last rider.
narration.17: If a rider already arrived at that exact minute, you cannot use it.
narration.19: Compare against the previous boarded rider next.
narration.21: This minute is free and still gets you a seat.
